ACCRPM.overview: ACCRPM (DoNotAllowAcToEngageAboveThisRPM_4000) provides critical mechanical over-speed protection for the automotive air conditioning compressor (stock calibration = 0x3E80 = 4,000 RPM). Automotive reciprocating piston and rotary vane A/C compressors are designed for maximum operating speeds of ~4,000 to 5,000 engine RPM. Running an A/C compressor at 6,000 RPM causes extreme piston velocities, reed valve flutter, and catastrophic clutch bearing destruction. If engine speed exceeds ACCRPM, the ECU disengages the A/C compressor clutch immediately, re-engaging it only when engine speed falls back below 4,000 RPM.
ACCRPM.overview_markdown:
`ACCRPM` (DoNotAllowAcToEngageAboveThisRPM_4000) provides critical mechanical over-speed protection for the automotive air conditioning compressor (stock calibration = `0x3E80` = 4,000 RPM).

Automotive reciprocating piston and rotary vane A/C compressors are designed for maximum operating speeds of ~4,000 to 5,000 engine RPM. Running an A/C compressor at 6,000 RPM causes extreme piston velocities, reed valve flutter, and catastrophic clutch bearing destruction. If engine speed exceeds `ACCRPM`, the ECU disengages the A/C compressor clutch immediately, re-engaging it only when engine speed falls back below 4,000 RPM.
ACCRPM.tuners_guide: Compressor Longevity: Never raise ACCRPM above 4,500 RPM. Spinning a factory Sanden or Nippondenso compressor beyond 4,500 RPM frequently leads to thrown compressor belts, seized bearings, or blown shaft seals.
ACCRPM.tuners_guide_markdown: * **Compressor Longevity**: Never raise `ACCRPM` above 4,500 RPM. Spinning a factory Sanden or Nippondenso compressor beyond 4,500 RPM frequently leads to thrown compressor belts, seized bearings, or blown shaft seals.

* Evaluated inside `ControlAirConditioning_MM` at line 1781.
* Compares 16-bit `EngineRpm_HB` register against `ACCRPM`.
* If `EngineRpm > ACCRPM` (`bhi LCDF2`), de-energizes the A/C clutch relay.

; --- ControlAirConditioning_MM (T-LMv13.asm:1780-1782) ---

        cpx  ACCRPM_DoNotAllowAcToEngageAboveThisRPM_4000 ; Compare with high-RPM ceiling ($1180, data 0x3E80 = 4000 RPM)
        bhi  LCDF2                               ; If Engine RPM > 4000 RPM, CUT OUT A/C COMPRESSOR!

ACCRPM.calibration_notes: * **Double-Byte Precision**: Evaluated with 16-bit index register comparison (`cpx`).

ACCTIM.overview: ACCTIM (AcDelayFromStartRunTransfer) enforces a brief delay (stock calibration = 4 ticks / ~0.4 sec) following engine startup before the ECU allows the A/C compressor clutch to engage. When an engine starts with the dashboard A/C switch already ON, engaging the compressor clutch while the starter motor is disengaging and oil pressure is building would impose harsh mechanical shock on the starter drive and stall the engine. ACCTIM holds off A/C clutch activation until the engine has cleanly transitioned into run mode.
ACCTIM.overview_markdown:
`ACCTIM` (AcDelayFromStartRunTransfer) enforces a brief delay (stock calibration = 4 ticks / ~0.4 sec) following engine startup before the ECU allows the A/C compressor clutch to engage.

When an engine starts with the dashboard A/C switch already ON, engaging the compressor clutch while the starter motor is disengaging and oil pressure is building would impose harsh mechanical shock on the starter drive and stall the engine. `ACCTIM` holds off A/C clutch activation until the engine has cleanly transitioned into run mode.
ACCTIM.tuners_guide: Starter Protection: Retain stock setting. Gives the engine time to establish stable combustion before absorbing compressor load.
ACCTIM.tuners_guide_markdown: * **Starter Protection**: Retain stock setting. Gives the engine time to establish stable combustion before absorbing compressor load.

ACLRPM.overview: ACLRPM (DisableAcBelowThisRPM_500) provides an emergency anti-stall cutout for the air conditioning compressor clutch (calibrated around 500 RPM / 0xA2). If engine RPM collapses due to sudden brake lockup, clutch drag, or low idle instability, dragging a mechanical A/C compressor will instantly kill the engine. When engine speed drops below TargetIdleSpeed * (ACLRPM / 256), the ECU immediately de-energizes the A/C clutch relay, dumping compressor drag so the engine can catch and revive.
ACLRPM.overview_markdown:
`ACLRPM` (DisableAcBelowThisRPM_500) provides an emergency anti-stall cutout for the air conditioning compressor clutch (calibrated around 500 RPM / `0xA2`).

If engine RPM collapses due to sudden brake lockup, clutch drag, or low idle instability, dragging a mechanical A/C compressor will instantly kill the engine. When engine speed drops below `TargetIdleSpeed * (ACLRPM / 256)`, the ECU immediately de-energizes the A/C clutch relay, dumping compressor drag so the engine can catch and revive.
ACLRPM.tuners_guide: Anti-Stall Protection: Prevents stalling when coming to a panic stop with the A/C on. Big Camshaft Lope: If an aftermarket camshaft causes idle RPM to lope deeply, ensuring ACLRPM is set around 500 RPM keeps the compressor from short-cycling during idle loping.
ACLRPM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Anti-Stall Protection**: Prevents stalling when coming to a panic stop with the A/C on.
* **Big Camshaft Lope**: If an aftermarket camshaft causes idle RPM to lope deeply, ensuring `ACLRPM` is set around 500 RPM keeps the compressor from short-cycling during idle loping.
ACLRPM.operating_conditions:
* Evaluated inside subroutine `ControlAirConditioning_MM` at line 1757.
* Multiplied against `TargetIdleSpeed_HB` using 16-bit math (`mul16bit`).
* If `EngineRpm_HB < CalculatedCutout`, A/C clutch is disengaged.

technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- ControlAirConditioning_MM (T-LMv13.asm:1757-1763) ---
        ldaa ACLRPM_DisableAcBelowThisRPM_500    ; Load scaling fraction ($1159, data 0xA2)
        sei                                      
        staa Temp5                               
        ldd  TargetIdleSpeed_HB                  ; Multiply fraction * TargetIdleSpeed
        jsr  mul16bit                            
        cli                                      
        std  Temp0                               ; Temp0 contains minimum stall RPM threshold

ACLRPM.calibration_notes: * **Proportional Scaling**: Scales proportionally with target idle speed.

metadata.units: Engine Speed Scaling Factor (0xA2 = 162 decimal; approx 500 RPM)

ACLRST.overview: ACLRST (CruiseControlDeltaSpeedToResetAccFlag) defines the speed error delta threshold below which the ECU disengages accelerated cruise gain mode and returns to regular steady-state gain mode. When resuming cruise speed, the ECU operates in high-gain accelerated mode (VACACC) to pull the vehicle back up toward target speed rapidly. Once vehicle speed climbs close enough to the set speed such that the remaining deficit (Target_Speed - Current_Speed) is less than ACLRST (~2.5 MPH), the accelerated cruise flag is cleared. The controller switches back to VACREG, smoothly settling onto the target speed without overshooting.
ACLRST.overview_markdown:
`ACLRST` (CruiseControlDeltaSpeedToResetAccFlag) defines the speed error delta threshold below which the ECU disengages accelerated cruise gain mode and returns to regular steady-state gain mode.
        
When resuming cruise speed, the ECU operates in high-gain accelerated mode (`VACACC`) to pull the vehicle back up toward target speed rapidly. Once vehicle speed climbs close enough to the set speed such that the remaining deficit (`Target_Speed - Current_Speed`) is less than `ACLRST` (~2.5 MPH), the accelerated cruise flag is cleared. The controller switches back to `VACREG`, smoothly settling onto the target speed without overshooting.
ACLRST.tuners_guide: Resume Overshoot: If the vehicle consistently overshoots set speed when resuming, increase ACLRST to e.g. 0x07 or 0x08 (3.5 - 4.0 MPH). This forces the controller to drop out of accelerated gain earlier and settle smoothly. Resume Undershoot: If the car accelerates aggressively on resume but stalls out 2-3 MPH below set speed and takes forever to climb the last bit, decrease ACLRST slightly.
ACLRST.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Resume Overshoot**: If the vehicle consistently overshoots set speed when resuming, increase `ACLRST` to e.g. `0x07` or `0x08` (3.5 - 4.0 MPH). This forces the controller to drop out of accelerated gain earlier and settle smoothly.
* **Resume Undershoot**: If the car accelerates aggressively on resume but stalls out 2-3 MPH below set speed and takes forever to climb the last bit, decrease `ACLRST` slightly.

* Evaluated inside subroutine `CruiseControlSet` at line 2292.
* Active while the cruise system is in accelerated pull-up mode.
* When delta speed drops below `ACLRST`, the accelerated flag is reset to 0.

; --- CruiseControlSet (T-LMv13.asm:2292-2296) ---
        cmpb ACLRST_CruiseControlDeltaSpeedToResetAccFlag               ; Check if delta speed has narrowed within reset threshold ($143D, data 0x05)
        bcc  HoldAcceleratedMode                                        ; If delta speed still large, remain in accelerated mode
        bclr CruiseFlag1, #0x04                                         ; Clear accelerated cruise flag, return to VACREG

ACLRST.calibration_notes: * **Mode Transition Gate**: Controls the critical handover boundary between aggressive resume acceleration and calm cruising.

ACOUT.overview: ACOUT (DeltaAboveMinThrottleToCutOutAc) is the Wide Open Throttle (WOT) A/C cutout threshold (stock calibration = 133 counts / ~2.60V above learned idle MINTHR). When the driver pins the throttle to accelerate, pass a vehicle, or launch at the drag strip, the ECU temporarily disengages the A/C compressor clutch. This unloads 5 to 10 parasitic horsepower from the crankshaft, delivering 100% of engine power to the front wheels. Once the accelerator pedal is released back below ACOUT, the A/C clutch re-engages smoothly.
ACOUT.overview_markdown:
`ACOUT` (DeltaAboveMinThrottleToCutOutAc) is the Wide Open Throttle (WOT) A/C cutout threshold (stock calibration = 133 counts / ~2.60V above learned idle `MINTHR`).

When the driver pins the throttle to accelerate, pass a vehicle, or launch at the drag strip, the ECU temporarily disengages the A/C compressor clutch. This unloads 5 to 10 parasitic horsepower from the crankshaft, delivering 100% of engine power to the front wheels. Once the accelerator pedal is released back below `ACOUT`, the A/C clutch re-engages smoothly.
ACOUT.tuners_guide: Passing Power: Stock value 0x85 cuts the A/C at ~75% throttle. Lowering ACOUT to 0x60 cuts the A/C sooner (at ~50% throttle), giving a sportier, more responsive feel during mid-throttle passing maneuvers.
ACOUT.tuners_guide_markdown: * **Passing Power**: Stock value `0x85` cuts the A/C at ~75% throttle. Lowering `ACOUT` to `0x60` cuts the A/C sooner (at ~50% throttle), giving a sportier, more responsive feel during mid-throttle passing maneuvers.
ACOUT.operating_conditions:
* Evaluated inside `ControlAirConditioning_MM` at line 1778.
* Subtracts `MINTHR_LowestSessionTPS` from `TpsVolts`.
* If `DeltaTPS >= ACOUT` (`bcc LCDEE`), the A/C clutch relay is commanded OFF.

technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- ControlAirConditioning_MM (T-LMv13.asm:1776-1779) ---
        subb MINTHR_LowestSessionTPS             ; Calculate throttle delta above idle
        bcs  LCDDF                               
        cmpb ACOUT_DeltaAboveMinThrottleToCutOutAc ; Compare against WOT cutout threshold ($1166, data 0x85)
        bcc  LCDEE                               ; If DeltaTPS >= ACOUT, DISENGAGE A/C CLUTCH!

ACOUT.calibration_notes: * **Instant Re-Engagement Cushion**: Controlled through transitional timers to avoid belt squeal.

metadata.units: TPS ADC Counts (0x85 = 133 counts; approx 2.60 Volts above MINTHR)

AKI1OF.overview: AKI1OF (AlkyInj1OffSetpointFromMAP) specifies the MAP threshold where the Stage 1 water/methanol solenoid shuts off as manifold pressure drops. Provides hysteresis cutoff protection for Stage 1 water/methanol injection, ensuring the nozzle snaps closed cleanly when throttle lifts occur.
AKI1OF.overview_markdown:
`AKI1OF` (AlkyInj1OffSetpointFromMAP) specifies the MAP threshold where the Stage 1 water/methanol solenoid shuts off as manifold pressure drops.
        
Provides hysteresis cutoff protection for Stage 1 water/methanol injection, ensuring the nozzle snaps closed cleanly when throttle lifts occur.
AKI1OF.tuners_guide: Staggering: Calibrate AKI1OF approximately 1.5 - 2.0 psi below AKI1ON. Ensures clean cutoff without premature shutoff during boost ramping.
AKI1OF.tuners_guide_markdown: * **Staggering**: Calibrate `AKI1OF` approximately 1.5 - 2.0 psi below `AKI1ON`. Ensures clean cutoff without premature shutoff during boost ramping.

AKI1ON.overview: AKI1ON (AlkyInj1OnSetpointFromMAP) sets the manifold pressure threshold where the Stage 1 water/methanol injection nozzle solenoid opens. In a staged water/methanol injection system, Stage 1 introduces a small, finely atomized spray nozzle into the charge pipe at moderate boost levels (e.g. 7-10 psi) to suppress initial intake air temperatures and prevent detonation as cylinder pressure begins climbing.
AKI1ON.overview_markdown:
`AKI1ON` (AlkyInj1OnSetpointFromMAP) sets the manifold pressure threshold where the Stage 1 water/methanol injection nozzle solenoid opens.
        
In a staged water/methanol injection system, Stage 1 introduces a small, finely atomized spray nozzle into the charge pipe at moderate boost levels (e.g. 7-10 psi) to suppress initial intake air temperatures and prevent detonation as cylinder pressure begins climbing.
AKI1ON.tuners_guide: Stage 1 Activation: Calibrate AKI1ON to trigger at the boost level where engine knock margin begins to narrow on pump gas (typically 7 to 10 psi boost). Nozzle Sizing: Size Stage 1 nozzle for approximately 10-15% of total fuel flow to avoid rich bogging.
AKI1ON.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Stage 1 Activation**: Calibrate `AKI1ON` to trigger at the boost level where engine knock margin begins to narrow on pump gas (typically 7 to 10 psi boost).
* **Nozzle Sizing**: Size Stage 1 nozzle for approximately 10-15% of total fuel flow to avoid rich bogging.

Closes the high-flow Stage 2 nozzle when manifold pressure falls below the calibrated hysteresis threshold, preserving water/methanol fluid and preventing over-rich fueling as boost begins tapering.

AKI2ON.overview: AKI2ON (AlkyInj2OnSetpointFromMAP) establishes the trigger threshold for the high-flow Stage 2 water/methanol injection nozzle solenoid. Under maximum boost conditions (e.g. 15-25+ psi), engine thermal loading and octane demand escalate drastically. AKI2ON activates a secondary high-volume methanol nozzle, delivering supplemental fuel volume, charge cooling, and high octane equivalent to support elevated boost without detonation.
AKI2ON.overview_markdown:
`AKI2ON` (AlkyInj2OnSetpointFromMAP) establishes the trigger threshold for the high-flow Stage 2 water/methanol injection nozzle solenoid.
        
Under maximum boost conditions (e.g. 15-25+ psi), engine thermal loading and octane demand escalate drastically. `AKI2ON` activates a secondary high-volume methanol nozzle, delivering supplemental fuel volume, charge cooling, and high octane equivalent to support elevated boost without detonation.
AKI2ON.tuners_guide: High Boost Staging: Set AKI2ON 4-8 psi higher than AKI1ON (e.g. Stage 1 at 8 psi, Stage 2 at 16 psi). This two-stage delivery provides linear octane supplementation without drowning the motor at mid-range boost.

AKPMOF.overview: AKPMOF (AlkyPumpOffSetpointFromMAP) establishes the shut-off MAP threshold for the water/methanol injection pump. Once the water/methanol pump has been energized at AKPMON, AKPMOF creates a pressure hysteresis cushion. As the driver lifts off the throttle and boost falls below AKPMOF, the pump driver de-energizes. This hysteresis deadband prevents the pump relay from buzzing or cycling rapidly if manifold pressure fluctuates near the trigger point.
AKPMOF.overview_markdown:
`AKPMOF` (AlkyPumpOffSetpointFromMAP) establishes the shut-off MAP threshold for the water/methanol injection pump.
        
Once the water/methanol pump has been energized at `AKPMON`, `AKPMOF` creates a pressure hysteresis cushion. As the driver lifts off the throttle and boost falls below `AKPMOF`, the pump driver de-energizes. This hysteresis deadband prevents the pump relay from buzzing or cycling rapidly if manifold pressure fluctuates near the trigger point.
AKPMOF.tuners_guide: Hysteresis Calibration: Set AKPMOF approximately 1.5 - 2.0 psi below AKPMON. For example, if the pump turns on at 5 psi boost, set it to turn off at 3 psi boost. Smooth Cutoff: Prevents sudden pump shutdown on momentary boost fluctuations during gear shifts.
AKPMOF.tuners_guide_markdown:

CLOTHR.overview: CLOTHR (CruiseControlDontVentIfThrottleBelowThis) specifies the minimum throttle angle floor below which the cruise vent solenoid is completely inhibited from firing. When vehicle speed exceeds set speed going down a steep hill, the vent solenoid bleeds vacuum to close the throttle. Once the throttle butterfly has returned completely to its closed idle stop position, further venting cannot slow the car down any more (the mechanical throttle is already at 0%). Pulsing the vent solenoid when the throttle is already fully closed accomplishes nothing except causing rapid wear on the solenoid valve and producing annoying clicking sounds under the hood. CLOTHR gates the vent circuit, shutting off the vent solenoid whenever the throttle is closed below this floor.

FANBAT.overview: FANBAT (FanTurnsOnWhenBatteryTempAboveThis) defines an underhood temperature threshold (stock calibration = 0x9A / ~120 degF) measured by the battery tray thermistor. Turbocharged engines radiate immense underhood heat soak from the exhaust manifold and turbo turbine housing. If the battery and ECU (which sits inside the Power Module behind the battery) reach extreme temperatures, lead-acid battery plates warp, and alternator field regulators lose efficiency. If battery temperature rises above FANBAT, the ECU turns the cooling fan ON to flush stagnant hot air out of the engine bay.

FANMAP.overview: FANMAP (FanTurnsOnWhenMapAboveBaroPlusThis) is a specialized performance feature (stock calibration = 0x1A / ~3.2 psi of boost above baro) that energizes the radiator cooling fan during sustained turbo boost. In factory turbocharged Chrysler applications (such as Daytona Shelby Z and GLHS models), the radiator and intercooler share the forward front-end airflow pathway. During hard acceleration or boost spool-up, charging the intercooler creates localized heat soak. When manifold boost exceeds barometric pressure by FANMAP ( MapValue >= BaroPressure + FANMAP ), the ECU turns the cooling fan ON immediately to draw extra airflow through the nose of the vehicle, lowering intake charge temperatures.

During hard acceleration or boost spool-up, charging the intercooler creates localized heat soak. When manifold boost exceeds barometric pressure by `FANMAP` ($	ext{MapValue} \ge 	ext{BaroPressure} + 	ext{FANMAP}$), the ECU turns the cooling fan ON immediately to draw extra airflow through the nose of the vehicle, lowering intake charge temperatures.

Eliminating Fan Cycling: If you do not want the fan cycling on boost, set FANMAP to 0xFF.

FANTMP1.overview: FANTMP1 (FanTurnOnTempAbove45Mph) defines the radiator cooling fan turn-on temperature threshold (stock calibration = 0xEE / ~218 degF) when the vehicle is cruising at highway speeds (above 45 MPH). At highway cruising speeds, high-velocity ambient ram-air naturally flows through the front grille, condenser, and radiator core, providing substantial passive cooling without requiring electrical fan assistance. Running the high-amp electric cooling fan at 60 MPH creates aerodynamic drag through the radiator shroud and places unnecessary electrical load on the alternator. FANTMP1 elevates the fan turn-on threshold to 218 degF at speed, ensuring the electric fan only engages on the highway if the engine encounters severe heat distress (such as climbing steep mountain grades or towing a trailer).

High-Speed Overheating: If the car runs cool in city traffic but temperatures climb on the highway, verify that FANTMP1 is set appropriately to assist ram airflow if the radiator core is partially clogged or heat-soaked.

FANTMP2.overview: FANTMP2 (FanTurnOffTempAbove45Mph) establishes the radiator cooling fan turn-OFF temperature threshold (stock calibration = 0xE8 / ~208 degF) when cruising above 45 MPH. Once high-speed coolant temperature triggers the fan ON (FANTMP1 at 218 degF), the fan continues running until ram airflow and forced convection pull engine coolant down below FANTMP2. The 10 degF hysteresis deadband between FANTMP1 (218 degF) and FANTMP2 (208 degF) prevents the heavy-duty radiator fan relay from rapidly chattering on and off.

Thermostat Floor: Never set FANTMP2 below the opening temperature of your mechanical thermostat (e.g. never set below 185 degF for a 180 degF thermostat), otherwise the electric fan will run continuously and never turn off on the highway!

FANTMP3.overview: FANTMP3 (FanTurnOnTempBelow35Mph) is the primary low-speed and curb idle radiator fan turn-on threshold (stock calibration = 0xE3 / ~200 degF). When driving in slow city traffic, waiting at stoplights, or idling in gridlock ( < 35 MPH), there is virtually zero passive ram airflow through the front fascia. Engine waste heat rapidly accumulates in the radiator coolant. When coolant temperature reaches FANTMP3, the ECU grounds the cooling fan relay driver, initiating forced airflow through the radiator core and condenser to bring engine temperature under control.
FANTMP3.overview_markdown:
`FANTMP3` (FanTurnOnTempBelow35Mph) is the primary low-speed and curb idle radiator fan turn-on threshold (stock calibration = `0xE3` / ~200°F).

Engine waste heat rapidly accumulates in the radiator coolant. When coolant temperature reaches `FANTMP3`, the ECU grounds the cooling fan relay driver, initiating forced airflow through the radiator core and condenser to bring engine temperature under control.
FANTMP3.tuners_guide: Most Important Fan Setting: FANTMP3 is the parameter tuners adjust most frequently to control hot idle temperatures. 180 degF Thermostat Setup: Lower FANTMP3 from stock ~200 degF (0xE3) down to 0xCB (~188 degF). 160 degF Thermostat Setup: Lower FANTMP3 to 0xB5 (~172 degF). Summer Traffic Knock Resistance: Keeping city idle coolant temperatures around 185 degF - 190 degF prevents heat-soak of the intake manifold, sharply reducing tip-in knock when accelerating away from stoplights.

KNKMIN.overview: KNKMIN (FlashCEMinTemp) defines the minimum engine coolant temperature required before the ECU will flash the instrument cluster "Check Engine" / "Power Loss" light upon detecting spark knock. Turbonator firmware features real-time knock indication: whenever the knock sensor detects detonation and the ECU pulls spark timing on any individual cylinder (Cylinder1-4Retard), the ECU flashes the Check Engine light to alert the driver immediately. However, forged pistons or cold engine blocks naturally exhibit mechanical piston slap and valve train clatter when cold. If knock indication were enabled on a cold motor, the driver would see constant false alarm flashing. KNKMIN blocks knock CEL flashing until the engine warms up to normal operating temperature (~160 degF).

LOSPCO.overview: LOSPCO (CruiseControlLowSpeedCutoutSpeed) establishes the absolute low-speed safety cutout threshold (approx 25 MPH) below which active cruise control will automatically disengage and shut down. If vehicle speed drops precipitously while cruise is active (for example, coming to a sudden stop in traffic, locking up tires in rain/snow, or spinning the vehicle), LOSPCO immediately disengages the system. Unlike MINSET which prevents arming below 30 MPH, LOSPCO monitors vehicle speed during active cruising; if speed ever drops below LOSPCO (~25 MPH), the cruise logic instantly dumps vacuum and returns control to the driver.

MAXSET.overview: MAXSET (CruiseControlMaxSetSpeedTimesTwo) enforces the maximum legal road speed at which the cruise control system is permitted to be engaged. For highway safety and federal motor vehicle safety regulations, cruise control is restricted from engaging at extreme vehicle speeds. In the Chrysler logic module, vehicle speed is represented in internal counts where Value = MPH * 2. Stock MAXSET is calibrated to 0xAA (170 decimal), corresponding to an exact maximum set speed limit of 85 MPH (170 / 2). If the driver attempts to press SET or RESUME at speeds above MAXSET, the ECU ignores the command.
MAXSET.overview_markdown:
`MAXSET` (CruiseControlMaxSetSpeedTimesTwo) enforces the maximum legal road speed at which the cruise control system is permitted to be engaged.
        
For highway safety and federal motor vehicle safety regulations, cruise control is restricted from engaging at extreme vehicle speeds. In the Chrysler logic module, vehicle speed is represented in internal counts where `Value = MPH * 2`. Stock `MAXSET` is calibrated to `0xAA` (170 decimal), corresponding to an exact maximum set speed limit of **85 MPH** (170 / 2). If the driver attempts to press SET or RESUME at speeds above `MAXSET`, the ECU ignores the command.
MAXSET.tuners_guide: Extended Highway Cruising: For western US states or track transport where legal speed limits reach 80 MPH, drivers wanting to cruise at 85-90 MPH can raise MAXSET to 0xBE (95 MPH) or 0xC8 (100 MPH). Speed Clamping: If vehicle speed exceeds MAXSET during an acceleration tap, set speed clamps at MAXSET / 2.
MAXSET.tuners_guide_markdown:

MAXTHR.overview: MAXTHR (CruiseControlDontVacIfThrottleAboveThis) establishes the maximum throttle angle ceiling allowed under cruise control operation. The factory vacuum cruise actuator is designed for modest cruising throttle adjustments. If the vehicle encounters a severe hill or load requiring more than ~30-35% throttle, pulling full vacuum to wide open throttle could cause uncontrollable runaway acceleration if a mechanical vacuum valve were to stick. Furthermore, operating a turbocharged engine at high boost under automated cruise control could result in dangerous engine conditions without driver awareness. MAXTHR places an absolute electronic clamp on vacuum pull; once throttle position reaches MAXTHR, no additional vacuum is commanded.

Furthermore, operating a turbocharged engine at high boost under automated cruise control could result in dangerous engine conditions without driver awareness. `MAXTHR` places an absolute electronic clamp on vacuum pull; once throttle position reaches `MAXTHR`, no additional vacuum is commanded.
MAXTHR.tuners_guide: Steep Mountain Grades: In hilly terrain, if the car loses speed on steep grades because cruise stops pulling at ~30% throttle, tuners can raise MAXTHR to 0x60 or 0x70 to give the cruise system more authority to hold speed. Safety Margin: Do not raise MAXTHR all the way to 100% (WOT). Maintaining a reasonable ceiling prevents runaway conditions and avoids entering high boost under cruise control.

MINSET.overview: MINSET (CruiseControlMinSetSpeedTimesTwo) defines the minimum low-speed cutoff threshold for cruise control operation. Cruise control is strictly designed for highway and open-road use. Using cruise control in city traffic, school zones, or residential areas represents a significant safety hazard. Stock MINSET is set to 0x3C (60 decimal), enforcing a strict minimum engagement threshold of 30 MPH (60 / 2). Any attempt to engage cruise below 30 MPH is immediately locked out by the ECU.

Stock `MINSET` is set to `0x3C` (60 decimal), enforcing a strict minimum engagement threshold of **30 MPH** (60 / 2). Any attempt to engage cruise below 30 MPH is immediately locked out by the ECU.
MINSET.tuners_guide: Factory Setting: 30 MPH is the standard factory minimum set speed. It is strongly recommended to keep MINSET at stock 0x3C (30 MPH) for public road safety.

PURHYS.overview: PURHYS (CannisterPurgeBaroHysteresis) provides a 2-count (~0.4 inHg) hysteresis deadband for canister purge control. When driving at light throttle near atmospheric pressure, manifold vacuum naturally fluctuates due to road bumps and subtle pedal adjustments. PURMAP.overview: PURMAP (CannisterPurgeWhenBelowThisBaro) establishes the intake manifold vacuum threshold (stock calibration = 0x05 / ~1.0 inHg vacuum below baro) required to energize the evaporative emission canister purge solenoid. Evaporative purge pulls fuel vapors from the charcoal canister directly into the intake plenum. Under boost or near wide-open throttle, manifold pressure is positive (boost), which would blow boost pressure backwards through the purge lines into the gas tank! PURMAP requires manifold pressure to be strictly below atmospheric pressure ( MapValue < Baro - PURMAP ) before the purge solenoid is allowed to open.

Under boost or near wide-open throttle, manifold pressure is positive (boost), which would blow boost pressure backwards through the purge lines into the gas tank! `PURMAP` requires manifold pressure to be strictly below atmospheric pressure ($	ext{MapValue} < 	ext{Baro} - 	ext{PURMAP}$) before the purge solenoid is allowed to open.
PURMAP.tuners_guide: Boost Check Valve Integrity: Turbo cars have one-way check valves on the canister purge line, but PURMAP provides software protection by shutting the solenoid off before manifold pressure reaches atmospheric zero. Shift Light Mod: When bit 4 of CONFIG is enabled, the Purge Solenoid output is repurposed to drive an RPM Shift Light!

RESTBL.overview: RESTBL (CruiseControlAdditionalSetupPulseForResume_FromSpeedDifference) specifies an additional vacuum setup pulse added to the base setup pulse when the driver engages "RESUME". When resuming cruise from a speed lower than the memorized target, the engine requires immediate additional throttle authority beyond a standard steady-state SET engagement. RESTBL calculates extra vacuum duration proportional to the deficit between current road speed and the stored target speed, pre-charging the servo bellows aggressively to begin pulling the vehicle back up to speed immediately.

RESTBL.tuners_guide: Resume Hesitation: If tapping Resume produces an initial hesitation before the car begins accelerating, increase RESTBL. Resume Kick: If hitting Resume causes an uncomfortably sharp jerk of the throttle, decrease the lower slope of RESTBL.

REVLMTX2.overview: REVLMTX2 (StagingModFuelShutoff) establishes the secondary hysteresis recovery threshold for the Turbonator 2-step staging limiter. REVLMTX defines where fuel cut initiates, and REVLMTX2 (located at offset +2 from REVLMTX) defines the recovery period where fuel resumes. REVLMTX.overview: REVLMTX (StagingModFuelShutoff) defines the primary engine speed setpoint for the Turbonator 2-step staging launch limiter. When sitting stationary at the starting tree with the staging switch activated (e.g. clutch pedal depressed or launch button held), the ECU compares distributor period against REVLMTX. When engine RPM reaches this threshold, the ECU cuts injector fuel pulses. This holds engine speed perfectly steady at the calibrated launch RPM (e.g. 3,300 - 3,800 RPM), allowing the exhaust pulses and ignition anti-lag retard to build several pounds of launch boost on the starting line before the clutch is released.

RVLSPS.overview: RVLSPS (Staging) defines the vehicle speed cutoff threshold for the Turbonator 2-step staging launch rev limiter. When staging at the drag strip starting line, the driver wants an aggressive low-RPM rev limit (e.g. 3,300 RPM) to spool the turbocharger against the brakes without over-revving. However, the moment the vehicle launches and rolls off the starting line, normal high-RPM power is required immediately. RVLSPS sets the road speed threshold (stock = 4 MPH): while vehicle speed is below RVLSPS, the staging limiter remains active; once the car exceeds this speed, the ECU automatically hands over to the primary high-RPM engine rev limiter (REVLMT).

RVLSWS.overview: RVLSWS (StagingLimiterSwitchSelect) selects the physical hardware switch input used to arm and activate the Turbonator 2-step staging launch limiter. T-LM allows flexible configuration of the launch limiter arming trigger: 0x00: Speed-only arming (active automatically whenever vehicle speed is below RVLSPS). 0x08 (Stock default): Clutch pedal switch input (Port C Bit 3). RVLSWS.overview_markdown:
`RVLSWS` (StagingLimiterSwitchSelect) selects the physical hardware switch input used to arm and activate the Turbonator 2-step staging launch limiter.
        
T-LM allows flexible configuration of the launch limiter arming trigger:
* `0x00`: Speed-only arming (active automatically whenever vehicle speed is below `RVLSPS`).
* `0x08` (Stock default): Clutch pedal switch input (Port C Bit 3). Limiter engages only when the clutch pedal is pressed to the floor.
* Custom bitmasks allow mapping to a momentary steering wheel launch button, line-lock switch, or emergency brake switch.
RVLSWS.tuners_guide: Manual Transmission (Clutch Switch): Leave at default 0x08. The 2-step arms when staged with the clutch depressed, and disengages the instant the clutch pedal begins releasing. Automatic Transmission (Brake / Line-Lock): Wire a momentary line-lock button to the brake/clutch switch sense pin, allowing automatic cars to stall the converter against the brake at the staging line. No Switch Setup: Setting RVLSWS to 0x00 enables pure speed mode; whenever the car is stopped ( < 4 MPH), the 2-step is armed.
RVLSWS.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Manual Transmission (Clutch Switch)**: Leave at default `0x08`. The 2-step arms when staged with the clutch depressed, and disengages the instant the clutch pedal begins releasing.
* **Automatic Transmission (Brake / Line-Lock)**: Wire a momentary line-lock button to the brake/clutch switch sense pin, allowing automatic cars to stall the converter against the brake at the staging line.
* **No Switch Setup**: Setting `RVLSWS` to `0x00` enables pure speed mode; whenever the car is stopped ($< 4$ MPH), the 2-step is armed.

SETIME.overview: SETIME (CruiseControlNoSetupPulseWhenDecelTimerAboveThis) establishes the upper timer limit for inhibiting the initial vacuum setup pulse during vehicle deceleration. If the driver has been holding down the "COAST / DECEL" cruise switch button and releases it to set a new lower cruise speed, the vehicle is actively decelerating. Applying a standard aggressive setup pulse immediately upon switch release would cause the car to lurch forward abruptly. SETIME checks the deceleration elapsed timer; if the timer is above this limit, the ECU suppresses or modifies the setup pulse to ensure smooth engagement at the new lower speed.

SETPW.overview: SETPW (CruiseControlSetupPulseForSet_FromSpeed) determines the initial "setup pulse" duration applied to the vacuum servo the instant the driver presses the "SET" button. Before cruise engages, the vacuum servo bellows is completely vented to atmospheric pressure and the throttle is held solely by the driver's foot. When "SET" is pressed, the ECU must instantly pre-charge the bellows with engine vacuum to take over the mechanical throttle load before the driver lifts off the gas pedal. SETPW scales this pre-charge pulse against vehicle speed, ensuring seamless handoff from foot throttle to cruise control without a momentary deceleration dip.
SETPW.overview_markdown:
`SETPW` (CruiseControlSetupPulseForSet_FromSpeed) determines the initial "setup pulse" duration applied to the vacuum servo the instant the driver presses the "SET" button.
        
Before cruise engages, the vacuum servo bellows is completely vented to atmospheric pressure and the throttle is held solely by the driver's foot. When "SET" is pressed, the ECU must instantly pre-charge the bellows with engine vacuum to take over the mechanical throttle load before the driver lifts off the gas pedal. `SETPW` scales this pre-charge pulse against vehicle speed, ensuring seamless handoff from foot throttle to cruise control without a momentary deceleration dip.
SETPW.tuners_guide: Set-Speed Sag / Dip: If releasing the accelerator pedal right after hitting SET causes the car to momentarily sag or lose 1-2 MPH, increase SETPW at that speed. Set-Speed Surge: If the car surges forward with unexpected acceleration when tapping SET, reduce SETPW.
SETPW.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Set-Speed Sag / Dip**: If releasing the accelerator pedal right after hitting SET causes the car to momentarily sag or lose 1-2 MPH, increase `SETPW` at that speed.

metadata.units: Vacuum Servo Pre-charge Pulse (ms) vs. Vehicle Road Speed

SETPW.raw_text: OVERVIEW: SETPW (CruiseControlSetupPulseForSet_FromSpeed) determines the initial "setup pulse" duration applied to the vacuum servo the instant the driver presses the "SET" button. Before cruise engages, the vacuum servo bellows is completely vented to atmospheric pressure and the throttle is held solely by the driver's foot. When "SET" is pressed, the ECU must instantly pre-charge the bellows with engine vacuum to take over the mechanical throttle load before the driver lifts off the gas pedal. SETPW scales this pre-charge pulse against vehicle speed, ensuring seamless handoff from foot throttle to cruise control without a momentary deceleration dip. | TUNER'S GUIDE: Set-Speed Sag / Dip: If releasing the accelerator pedal right after hitting SET causes the car to momentarily sag or lose 1-2 MPH, increase SETPW at that speed. Set-Speed Surge: If the car surges forward with unexpected acceleration when tapping SET, reduce SETPW.

SLRPM.overview: SLRPM (ShiftLightSetpoint) sets the precise engine RPM at which the ECU illuminates the instrument cluster upshift indicator or an external shift light. Turbonator code repurposes the purge/EGR driver output or the factory cluster upshift arrow to function as a programmable high-RPM shift light. When engine speed climbs to SLRPM, the ECU grounds the driver circuit, illuminating the shift light to tell the driver to shift before hitting the rev limiter. Once RPM drops below SLRPM during gear change, the light turns off immediately.
SLRPM.overview_markdown:
`SLRPM` (ShiftLightSetpoint) sets the precise engine RPM at which the ECU illuminates the instrument cluster upshift indicator or an external shift light.
        
Turbonator code repurposes the purge/EGR driver output or the factory cluster upshift arrow to function as a programmable high-RPM shift light. When engine speed climbs to `SLRPM`, the ECU grounds the driver circuit, illuminating the shift light to tell the driver to shift before hitting the rev limiter. Once RPM drops below `SLRPM` during gear change, the light turns off immediately.
SLRPM.tuners_guide: Power Peak Shift Point: Set SLRPM roughly 200-400 RPM past peak horsepower on your dyno sheet, but 300-500 RPM below your hard rev limiter (REVLMT). This gives the driver human reaction time to initiate the shift without bouncing off the limiter. Stock Valvetrain Safety: On stock hydraulic lifter 8-valve engines, set SLRPM to 5,600 - 5,800 RPM to protect valvetrain components from valve float.
SLRPM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Power Peak Shift Point**: Set `SLRPM` roughly 200-400 RPM past peak horsepower on your dyno sheet, but 300-500 RPM below your hard rev limiter (`REVLMT`). This gives the driver human reaction time to initiate the shift without bouncing off the limiter.
* **Stock Valvetrain Safety**: On stock hydraulic lifter 8-valve engines, set `SLRPM` to 5,600 - 5,800 RPM to protect valvetrain components from valve float.

SPGAIN.overview: SPGAIN (CruiseControlSpeedGainFactor_FromSpeed) adjusts the overall cruise control servo gain as a function of vehicle road speed. Aerodynamic drag increases with the square of vehicle speed ( F_drag proportional to v^2 ). At 35 MPH, small throttle movements produce rapid speed changes, while at 75 MPH, substantial throttle movements are required to counter wind resistance. SPGAIN provides speed-dependent gain scheduling, scaling vacuum servo responsiveness across the vehicle's speed range to provide uniform control response from 35 MPH to 85 MPH.
SPGAIN.overview_markdown:
`SPGAIN` (CruiseControlSpeedGainFactor_FromSpeed) adjusts the overall cruise control servo gain as a function of vehicle road speed.
        
Aerodynamic drag increases with the square of vehicle speed ($F_{drag} \propto v^2$). At 35 MPH, small throttle movements produce rapid speed changes, while at 75 MPH, substantial throttle movements are required to counter wind resistance. `SPGAIN` provides speed-dependent gain scheduling, scaling vacuum servo responsiveness across the vehicle's speed range to provide uniform control response from 35 MPH to 85 MPH.
SPGAIN.tuners_guide: High-Speed Sluggishness: If cruise holds speed crisply at 45 MPH but feels soft and unresponsive at 75 MPH, increase SPGAIN at higher road speeds. Low-Speed Twitch: If cruise feels jumpy at 35-40 MPH, ensure SPGAIN gain is calibrated lower in the lower speed range.
SPGAIN.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **High-Speed Sluggishness**: If cruise holds speed crisply at 45 MPH but feels soft and unresponsive at 75 MPH, increase `SPGAIN` at higher road speeds.
* **Low-Speed Twitch**: If cruise feels jumpy at 35-40 MPH, ensure `SPGAIN` gain is calibrated lower in the lower speed range.

* Active across all cruise regulation cycles.

THGAIN.overview: THGAIN (CruiseControlThrottleGainFactor_FromThrottle) provides a nonlinear gain correction factor applied to cruise servo duty cycle based on the current throttle opening angle. Mechanical throttle linkages and butterfly throttle bodies are inherently progressive: a 1-degree rotation at 5% throttle allows a massive percentage change in airflow, whereas a 1-degree rotation at 40% throttle produces a much smaller change in airflow. THGAIN compensates for this progressive airflow response by adjusting servo pulse authority as a function of throttle position, linearizing cruise throttle control across the operational range.
THGAIN.overview_markdown:
`THGAIN` (CruiseControlThrottleGainFactor_FromThrottle) provides a nonlinear gain correction factor applied to cruise servo duty cycle based on the current throttle opening angle.
        
Mechanical throttle linkages and butterfly throttle bodies are inherently progressive: a 1-degree rotation at 5% throttle allows a massive percentage change in airflow, whereas a 1-degree rotation at 40% throttle produces a much smaller change in airflow. `THGAIN` compensates for this progressive airflow response by adjusting servo pulse authority as a function of throttle position, linearizing cruise throttle control across the operational range.
THGAIN.tuners_guide: Large Throttle Bodies: Aftermarket 52mm or 58mm throttle bodies flow significantly more air at small throttle angles than the stock 48mm unit. Flattening or reducing THGAIN at low throttle prevents cruise control twitchiness with oversized throttle bodies. High-Speed Hill Assist: Increasing THGAIN at higher throttle angles gives the cruise controller more authority to hold highway speeds up steep mountain passes.

* **Large Throttle Bodies**: Aftermarket 52mm or 58mm throttle bodies flow significantly more air at small throttle angles than the stock 48mm unit. Flattening or reducing `THGAIN` at low throttle prevents cruise control twitchiness with oversized throttle bodies.
* **High-Speed Hill Assist**: Increasing `THGAIN` at higher throttle angles gives the cruise controller more authority to hold highway speeds up steep mountain passes.

VACACC.overview: VACACC (CruiseControlVacAcceleratedGainCurve_FromDeltaSpeed) defines the high-gain vacuum servo pulse curve activated during large speed errors or when resuming vehicle speed. When the driver hits Resume from a significantly lower speed, or when encountering a steep incline that causes vehicle speed to drop past ACLRST, the ECU sets the accelerated cruise flag. In this mode, the cruise controller switches from VACREG to VACACC, delivering much larger vacuum solenoid pulse widths to forcefully pull the throttle open and accelerate the car back toward the target set speed rapidly.
VACACC.overview_markdown:
`VACACC` (CruiseControlVacAcceleratedGainCurve_FromDeltaSpeed) defines the high-gain vacuum servo pulse curve activated during large speed errors or when resuming vehicle speed.
        
When the driver hits Resume from a significantly lower speed, or when encountering a steep incline that causes vehicle speed to drop past `ACLRST`, the ECU sets the accelerated cruise flag. In this mode, the cruise controller switches from `VACREG` to `VACACC`, delivering much larger vacuum solenoid pulse widths to forcefully pull the throttle open and accelerate the car back toward the target set speed rapidly.
VACACC.tuners_guide: Resume Sluggishness: If resuming from 45 MPH to 65 MPH feels lethargic, increase the gain values in VACACC. Resume Overshoot: If the car aggressively overshoots the set speed upon resuming (e.g. climbing to 72 MPH before settling back to 65 MPH), reduce VACACC slope.
VACACC.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Resume Sluggishness**: If resuming from 45 MPH to 65 MPH feels lethargic, increase the gain values in `VACACC`.
* **Resume Overshoot**: If the car aggressively overshoots the set speed upon resuming (e.g. climbing to 72 MPH before settling back to 65 MPH), reduce `VACACC` slope.

VACREG.overview: VACREG (CruiseControlVacRegularGainGurve_FromDeltaSpeed) defines the primary proportional vacuum servo gain curve used by the cruise control system under steady-state cruising. When road speed falls slightly below the target set speed (e.g. encountering a moderate highway grade or headwind), the ECU calculates the delta speed error (Target_Speed - Current_Speed). VACREG maps this speed deficit into a proportional vacuum solenoid pulse width. Applying vacuum draws on the throttle actuator diaphragm, opening the throttle blade smoothly to restore the target cruising speed without hunting or surging.
VACREG.overview_markdown:
`VACREG` (CruiseControlVacRegularGainGurve_FromDeltaSpeed) defines the primary proportional vacuum servo gain curve used by the cruise control system under steady-state cruising.
        
When road speed falls slightly below the target set speed (e.g. encountering a moderate highway grade or headwind), the ECU calculates the delta speed error (`Target_Speed - Current_Speed`). `VACREG` maps this speed deficit into a proportional vacuum solenoid pulse width. Applying vacuum draws on the throttle actuator diaphragm, opening the throttle blade smoothly to restore the target cruising speed without hunting or surging.
VACREG.tuners_guide: Speed Droop on Hills: If the vehicle loses 2-4 MPH on highway hills before recovering, increase the upper points of VACREG to command more aggressive vacuum pull. Throttle Surging / Hunting: If the cruise control oscillates or pulses the accelerator pedal while driving on flat roads, reduce the slope of VACREG around zero delta speed.
VACREG.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Speed Droop on Hills**: If the vehicle loses 2-4 MPH on highway hills before recovering, increase the upper points of `VACREG` to command more aggressive vacuum pull.
* **Throttle Surging / Hunting**: If the cruise control oscillates or pulses the accelerator pedal while driving on flat roads, reduce the slope of `VACREG` around zero delta speed.

VENTRG.overview: VENTRG (CruiseControlVentRegularGainCurve_FromDeltaSpeed) establishes the vent solenoid pulse duration gain curve used to bleed vacuum from the cruise servo when vehicle speed exceeds the set target. When descending a highway incline or following an acceleration event, vehicle speed rises above the target cruise setting (Current_Speed > Target_Speed). The ECU calculates the positive speed error and looks up VENTRG. The resulting pulse energizes the vent solenoid, venting vacuum from the actuator diaphragm to atmospheric pressure so the return spring pulls the throttle blade closed.
VENTRG.overview_markdown:
`VENTRG` (CruiseControlVentRegularGainCurve_FromDeltaSpeed) establishes the vent solenoid pulse duration gain curve used to bleed vacuum from the cruise servo when vehicle speed exceeds the set target.
        
When descending a highway incline or following an acceleration event, vehicle speed rises above the target cruise setting (`Current_Speed > Target_Speed`). The ECU calculates the positive speed error and looks up `VENTRG`. The resulting pulse energizes the vent solenoid, venting vacuum from the actuator diaphragm to atmospheric pressure so the return spring pulls the throttle blade closed.
VENTRG.tuners_guide: Downhill Speed Creep: If the vehicle gains significant speed on downhill stretches with cruise engaged, increase VENTRG values to vent vacuum more aggressively. Throttle Jerkiness: Setting VENTRG excessively high causes the throttle to snap shut abruptly, inducing driveline lash on manual transmission vehicles.
VENTRG.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Downhill Speed Creep**: If the vehicle gains significant speed on downhill stretches with cruise engaged, increase `VENTRG` values to vent vacuum more aggressively.

VNTAB1.overview: VNTAB1 (CruiseControlLimitToAMaxVent) defines the maximum allowable pulse width duration limit for the cruise control vent solenoid. When the vehicle encounters an overspeed condition (e.g. cresting a hill), the vent solenoid opens to dump vacuum from the actuator. If the ECU vented vacuum too rapidly or held the vent open continuously, the throttle butterfly would slam shut abruptly against its idle stop, causing severe driveline bucking and passenger discomfort. VNTAB1 establishes an absolute clamp on single vent pulses, ensuring throttle retraction is smooth and controlled.

`VNTAB1` (CruiseControlLimitToAMaxVent) defines the maximum allowable pulse width duration limit for the cruise control vent solenoid.

If the ECU vented vacuum too rapidly or held the vent open continuously, the throttle butterfly would slam shut abruptly against its idle stop, causing severe driveline bucking and passenger discomfort. `VNTAB1` establishes an absolute clamp on single vent pulses, ensuring throttle retraction is smooth and controlled.
VNTAB1.tuners_guide: Factory Setting: Stock value is 0x70 (112 counts). Retain stock setting for factory vacuum actuator diaphragms. Lightweight Actuators: If using an aftermarket or smaller vacuum servo actuator that vents faster than stock, reducing VNTAB1 prevents harsh throttle closing.

VNTAB2.overview: VNTAB2 (CruiseControlLimitToHalfMaxVent) sets a intermediate threshold used to restrict vent solenoid pulses to half-maximum under mild overspeed conditions. When vehicle speed only moderately exceeds the set target, dumping full vent capacity would vent too much vacuum, causing the vehicle to undershoot set speed and begin an annoying oscillate/hunt cycle. VNTAB2 provides an intermediate throttling clamp, keeping the vent pulse gentle during minor speed corrections.

WOTBAT.overview: WOTBAT (WOTBatteryVoltsTarget) specifies the target battery regulation voltage commanded during Wide Open Throttle (WOT) acceleration. The Chrysler logic module directly controls alternator charging field duty cycle via an internal pulse-width modulated voltage regulator. An energized alternator charging at 14.5V under heavy electrical load can consume 3 to 5 engine horsepower. Under WOT acceleration, Turbonator code lowers the target charging voltage to WOTBAT (approx 12.5V - 12.8V). This effectively de-energizes the alternator field, shedding parasitic mechanical drag from the crankshaft and transferring every possible horsepower directly to the drive wheels during wide-open drag strip passes or passing maneuvers.

If running an exceptionally high-draw fuel pump without a dedicated booster, keep WOTBAT around 13.0V (0xF0) to prevent fuel pressure drop.

BSOLCO.overview: BSOLCO_BoostSolenoidCutout specifies the knock spark retard threshold above which the wastegate solenoid is completely de-energized (cut out). When severe knock occurs, the ECU initially retards ignition timing. If timing retard reaches BSOLCO ( 3.5 deg of retard), the ECU determines that timing retard alone cannot control the detonation. It immediately cuts power to the wastegate solenoid (0% duty cycle), dropping the turbocharger down to mechanical actuator spring pressure (approx. 5-7 psi).
BSOLCO.overview_markdown:
`BSOLCO_BoostSolenoidCutout` specifies the **knock spark retard threshold above which the wastegate solenoid is completely de-energized (cut out)**.

When severe knock occurs, the ECU initially retards ignition timing. If timing retard reaches `BSOLCO` ($3.5^\circ$ of retard), the ECU determines that timing retard alone cannot control the detonation. It immediately cuts power to the wastegate solenoid (0% duty cycle), dropping the turbocharger down to mechanical actuator spring pressure (approx. 5–7 psi).
BSOLCO.tuners_guide: Stock Value: 0x07 ( ~ 3.5 deg spark retard). Engine Protection: Immediate, physical boost cut to protect the head gasket and pistons if bad gasoline or extreme heat causes persistent detonation. Tuning Guidance: Do not raise excessively; cutting boost when knocking is the safest behavior possible on a turbocharged engine.
BSOLCO.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Stock Value:** `0x07` ($pprox 3.5^\circ$ spark retard).
* **Engine Protection:** Immediate, physical boost cut to protect the head gasket and pistons if bad gasoline or extreme heat causes persistent detonation.
* **Tuning Guidance:** Do not raise excessively; cutting boost when knocking is the safest behavior possible on a turbocharged engine.
BSOLCO.operating_conditions:
* **Solenoid Failsafe Cutout:**
  * In `ControlWastegate`:
  * Total knock retard (`TotalKnockRetard`) is compared against `BSOLCO`.
  * If `TotalKnockRetard >= BSOLCO`: The wastegate solenoid output is forced to 0% duty cycle (`staa BaseWastegateDutyCycle`).

        cmpa BSOLCO_BoostSolenoidCutout ; Compare with 0x07 (3.5 degrees)
        bcs  SkipSolenoidCutout ; If knock < BSOLCO, keep modulating solenoid!
        clra                 ; Force 0% wastegate duty cycle!
        staa BaseWastegateDutyCycle

BSTSWS.overview: BSTSWS_HighBoostSwitchSelect defines the hardware input pin bitmask used to toggle Turbonator Switchable Boost (High/Low Boost). Turbonator firmware allows the driver to toggle between a daily-driver "Low Boost" setting and a race "High Boost" setting using a dashboard switch or steering wheel button. BSTSWS selects which physical wire on Logic Module Connector B senses this toggle.
BSTSWS.overview_markdown:
`BSTSWS_HighBoostSwitchSelect` defines the **hardware input pin bitmask used to toggle Turbonator Switchable Boost (High/Low Boost)**.

Turbonator firmware allows the driver to toggle between a daily-driver "Low Boost" setting and a race "High Boost" setting using a dashboard switch or steering wheel button. `BSTSWS` selects which physical wire on Logic Module Connector B senses this toggle.
BSTSWS.tuners_guide: Pin Bitmask Assignments: 0x01: Cruise Set (Pin B9) 0x02: Cruise Resume (Pin B10 - Factory Default) 0x04: A/C Clutch Sense (Pin B11) 0x08: Park/Neutral (Pin B12) 0x10: Brake Switch (Pin B13) 0x40: Cruise Enable (Pin B15) Custom Toggle Switch: Wire a toggle switch between the chosen pin and ground/12V (matching polarity) to give instant dual-stage boost control.
BSTSWS.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Pin Bitmask Assignments:**
  * `0x01`: Cruise Set (Pin B9)
  * `0x02`: Cruise Resume (Pin B10 — Factory Default)
  * `0x04`: A/C Clutch Sense (Pin B11)
  * `0x08`: Park/Neutral (Pin B12)
  * `0x10`: Brake Switch (Pin B13)
  * `0x40`: Cruise Enable (Pin B15)
* **Custom Toggle Switch:** Wire a toggle switch between the chosen pin and ground/12V (matching polarity) to give instant dual-stage boost control.
BSTSWS.operating_conditions:
* **Switchable Boost Check:**
  * Enabled when `cfg_SwBoost` bit is set in `CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags`.
  * In `CalcTargetBoost_MM`:
  * Reads `Z83_PortCdata` and masks with `BSTSWS`.
  * If low boost is active, branches to `LoadLoBoost` to clamp target to `SWBSLO`.

technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
ldab Z83_PortCdata    ; Read Port C hardware input pins
        bita #cfg_BstSwPol    ; Check polarity bit
        beq  Polarity_Lo
Polarity_Hi:
        andb BSTSWS_HighBoostSwitchSelect ; Test chosen pin
        beq  NoLoBoost        ; If high, keep high boost!
        bra  LoadLoBoost      ; Else drop to low boost!

DCRPMH.overview: DCRPMH_NoWastegateDutyCycleCorrectionAboveThisRpm defines the upper engine speed threshold above which adaptive wastegate duty cycle correction is frozen. Chrysler's adaptive wastegate algorithm was designed specifically to learn and compensate for low-RPM spool-up variations (1504 RPM to 2528 RPM). Above 2528 RPM, the turbo is already fully spooled, so adaptive duty cycle learning freezes to avoid interference with high-RPM closed-loop regulation.

`DCRPMH_NoWastegateDutyCycleCorrectionAboveThisRpm` defines the **upper engine speed threshold above which adaptive wastegate duty cycle correction is frozen**.

DCRPMH.tuners_guide: Stock Value: 0x4F ( 2528 RPM ). Big Turbo Upgrades: Large turbos (e.g. Holset HX35, Garrett GT30R) spool later (often between 3000 and 4200 RPM). Raising DCRPMH to 0x80 ( 4096 RPM ) expands the adaptive spool-up learning window to match the spool RPM of the larger turbo.

DCWADJ.overview: DCWADJ_FullThrottleWastegateDutyCycleAdjustment_FromRpm provides an RPM-dependent duty cycle correction adder applied to the base wastegate duty cycle (DCWOT). Turbocharger volumetric efficiency and turbine backpressure change dramatically across the rev range. At low RPM, exhaust energy is weak and extra duty cycle is required to spool the turbo. At high RPM, rising exhaust manifold backpressure pushes the internal wastegate flapper open, often requiring progressive duty cycle addition to prevent boost from tapering off towards redline. DCWADJ curves the duty cycle across RPM.
DCWADJ.overview_markdown:
`DCWADJ_FullThrottleWastegateDutyCycleAdjustment_FromRpm` provides an **RPM-dependent duty cycle correction adder** applied to the base wastegate duty cycle (`DCWOT`).

Turbocharger volumetric efficiency and turbine backpressure change dramatically across the rev range. At low RPM, exhaust energy is weak and extra duty cycle is required to spool the turbo. At high RPM, rising exhaust manifold backpressure pushes the internal wastegate flapper open, often requiring progressive duty cycle addition to prevent boost from tapering off towards redline. `DCWADJ` curves the duty cycle across RPM.
DCWADJ.tuners_guide: Preventing High-RPM Boost Drop: Small stock turbos (Garrett T03 / Mitsubishi TE04H) frequently drop boost by 2-4 psi above 5000 RPM because exhaust backpressure overcomes the weak wastegate canister spring. Adding positive duty cycle in DCWADJ at 4800-6000 RPM compensates for this backpressure bleed and holds flat boost to redline.

* **Preventing High-RPM Boost Drop:**
  * Small stock turbos (Garrett T03 / Mitsubishi TE04H) frequently drop boost by 2–4 psi above 5000 RPM because exhaust backpressure overcomes the weak wastegate canister spring.

DCWADJ.operating_conditions:

  * In `ControlWastegate`:
  * Looked up vs `EngineRpm` and added algebraically (signed addition) to base duty cycle.

DCWOT.overview: DCWOT_FullThrottleWastegateDutyCycle_C8is100Percent_FromMap is the primary feed-forward (open-loop baseline) wastegate duty cycle curve used by the Chrysler boost control system. The Chrysler wastegate solenoid bleeds control pressure away from the wastegate actuator can: 0% Duty Cycle (Solenoid De-energized): Full boost pressure reaches the actuator canister, forcing the wastegate flapper open at base spring pressure (approx. 5.5 to 7.0 psi). 100% Duty Cycle (Solenoid Fully Pulsing / Venting): All pressure is bled off to atmosphere; the wastegate flapper stays held shut, producing maximum turbo spool. DCWOT maps target boost pressure to the expected solenoid duty cycle required to hold that boost level. Closed-loop corrections then trim this baseline.
DCWOT.overview_markdown:
`DCWOT_FullThrottleWastegateDutyCycle_C8is100Percent_FromMap` is the **primary feed-forward (open-loop baseline) wastegate duty cycle curve** used by the Chrysler boost control system.

The Chrysler wastegate solenoid bleeds control pressure away from the wastegate actuator can:
* **0% Duty Cycle (Solenoid De-energized):** Full boost pressure reaches the actuator canister, forcing the wastegate flapper open at base spring pressure (approx. 5.5 to 7.0 psi).
* **100% Duty Cycle (Solenoid Fully Pulsing / Venting):** All pressure is bled off to atmosphere; the wastegate flapper stays held shut, producing maximum turbo spool.

`DCWOT` maps target boost pressure to the expected solenoid duty cycle required to hold that boost level. Closed-loop corrections then trim this baseline.
DCWOT.tuners_guide: Scaling Mechanics: Duty cycle is scaled from 0 to 200 counts (0x00 = 0%, 0xC8 = 100%, 1 count = 0.5%). Tuning for Higher Boost: When raising boost targets in WSGRPM, you must ensure DCWOT provides sufficient duty cycle to hold that boost. If the turbo cannot reach target boost despite raising target tables, raise the duty cycle values in DCWOT. Actuator Spring Upgrades: If you install a stiffer aftermarket wastegate can (e.g. 10 psi spring instead of 5.5 psi spring), lower DCWOT across the board to prevent uncontrolled boost overshooting.
DCWOT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Scaling Mechanics:** Duty cycle is scaled from 0 to 200 counts (`0x00` = 0%, `0xC8` = 100%, `1 count = 0.5%`).
* **Tuning for Higher Boost:**
  * When raising boost targets in `WSGRPM`, you must ensure `DCWOT` provides sufficient duty cycle to hold that boost.
  * If the turbo cannot reach target boost despite raising target tables, raise the duty cycle values in `DCWOT`.
* **Actuator Spring Upgrades:** If you install a stiffer aftermarket wastegate can (e.g. 10 psi spring instead of 5.5 psi spring), lower `DCWOT` across the board to prevent uncontrolled boost overshooting.
DCWOT.operating_conditions:
* **Wide-Open Throttle Boost Delivery:**
  * In `ControlWastegate`:
  * When operating at full throttle, `TargetBoost` is looked up in `DCWOT`.
  * The resulting base duty cycle is combined with RPM adjustments (`DCWADJ`) and closed-loop feedback trims to set the final wastegate PWM output timer.

LF38A:  ldx  #DCWOT_FullThrottleWastegateDutyCycle_C8is100Percent_FromMap
        jsr  Lookup4ByteTable ; Look up base duty cycle from TargetBoost
        staa BaseWastegateDutyCycle

MPSHFA.overview: MPSHFA_OverboostFuelShutoffEnablePointFromMap_Absolute defines the instantaneous hard overboost ceiling offset. While moderate overboost (MPSHFT) waits for a delay timer to allow harmless momentary pressure spikes, extreme runaway overboost requires instant intervention. MPSHFA adds an absolute ceiling offset ( 3.0 psi ) above MPSHFT: if manifold pressure surpasses this combined absolute ceiling ( 13.6 + 3.0 = 16.6 psi ), the ECU instantly cuts fuel with zero timer delay.
MPSHFA.overview_markdown:
`MPSHFA_OverboostFuelShutoffEnablePointFromMap_Absolute` defines the **instantaneous hard overboost ceiling offset**.

While moderate overboost (`MPSHFT`) waits for a delay timer to allow harmless momentary pressure spikes, extreme runaway overboost requires instant intervention. `MPSHFA` adds an absolute ceiling offset ($3.0\text{ psi}$) above `MPSHFT`: if manifold pressure surpasses this combined absolute ceiling ($13.6 + 3.0 = 16.6\text{ psi}$), the ECU **instantly cuts fuel with zero timer delay**.
MPSHFA.tuners_guide: Stock Value: 0x1A ( 3.0 psi above MPSHFT). Absolute Failsafe: Hard stop protecting against catastrophic boost spikes. Tuning Guidance: When raising MPSHFT, ensure MPSHFA is adjusted appropriately, or set MPSHFT = 0xFF to disable both stages.
MPSHFA.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Stock Value:** `0x1A` ($3.0\text{ psi}$ above `MPSHFT`).
* **Absolute Failsafe:** Hard stop protecting against catastrophic boost spikes.
* **Tuning Guidance:** When raising `MPSHFT`, ensure `MPSHFA` is adjusted appropriately, or set `MPSHFT = 0xFF` to disable both stages.
MPSHFA.operating_conditions:
* **Instantaneous Cut Evaluation:**
  * In `ControlEngineCutout_MM`:
  * Compares `MapValue` with $(\text{Baro} + \text{MPSHFT} + \text{MPSHFA})$.
  * If `MapValue >= Absolute Threshold`: Fuel cut engages instantly (`bcs LEEBF`).

technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
adda MPSHFA_OverboostFuelShutoffEnablePointFromMap_Absolute ; Add 0x1A
        bcc  LEEB2
        ldaa #0xff
LEEB2:  cmpa MapValue       ; Compare with actual MAP
        bcs  LEEBF          ; If MAP >= Absolute Limit, CUT FUEL INSTANTLY!

MPSHFT.overview: MPSHFT_OverboostFuelShutoffEnablePointFromMap_Timer establishes the timed overboost fuel shutoff threshold. To prevent catastrophic engine destruction from an overboosting turbocharger (e.g. disconnected wastegate actuator hose or frozen wastegate flapper), the Chrysler ECU cuts fuel to all four injectors if boost pressure exceeds factory safety margins. MPSHFT defines the initial threshold ( 13.6 psi boost ): if boost exceeds this level, the ECU starts the overboost timer (TRNTIM). If boost does not fall below MPSHFT before the timer expires, the ECU cuts fuel completely.
MPSHFT.overview_markdown:
`MPSHFT_OverboostFuelShutoffEnablePointFromMap_Timer` establishes the **timed overboost fuel shutoff threshold**.

To prevent catastrophic engine destruction from an overboosting turbocharger (e.g. disconnected wastegate actuator hose or frozen wastegate flapper), the Chrysler ECU cuts fuel to all four injectors if boost pressure exceeds factory safety margins. `MPSHFT` defines the initial threshold ($13.6\text{ psi boost}$): if boost exceeds this level, the ECU starts the overboost timer (`TRNTIM`). If boost does not fall below `MPSHFT` before the timer expires, the ECU cuts fuel completely.
MPSHFT.tuners_guide: Stock Value: 0x76 ( 13.6 psig ). The "Hitting a Brick Wall" Sensation: When modifying a Chrysler turbo car with a manual bleed valve or aftermarket boost controller, hitting 14 psi triggers the overboost fuel cut, causing the car to violently buck forward. Raising for More Boost: When tuning for 15+ psi boost, you must raise MPSHFT (e.g. to 18-20 psi, or 0xFF to disable) so higher boost targets can be sustained.
MPSHFT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Stock Value:** `0x76` ($13.6\text{ psig}$).
* **The "Hitting a Brick Wall" Sensation:**
  * When modifying a Chrysler turbo car with a manual bleed valve or aftermarket boost controller, hitting 14 psi triggers the overboost fuel cut, causing the car to violently buck forward.
* **Raising for More Boost:**
  * When tuning for 15+ psi boost, you **must raise `MPSHFT`** (e.g. to 18–20 psi, or `0xFF` to disable) so higher boost targets can be sustained.
MPSHFT.operating_conditions:
* **Overboost Timer Evaluation:**
  * In `ControlEngineCutout_MM`:
  * Compares actual manifold pressure with $(\text{Baro} + \text{MPSHFT})$.
  * If $\text{MapValue} > (\text{Baro} + \text{MPSHFT})$: The overboost countdown timer (`Timer_FuelShutoff`) decrements toward zero.
  * If the timer reaches 0: Fuel shutoff flag is set, dropping injector pulse width to zero!
  * Setting `MPSHFT = 0xFF` disables timed overboost shutoff.

technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
LEEA0:  adda MPSHFT_OverboostFuelShutoffEnablePointFromMap_Timer ; Add 0x76 to Baro
        bcc  LEEA7
        ldaa #0xff          ; Clamp at 0xFF
LEEA7:  cmpa MapValue       ; Compare with current MAP
        bhi  LEECD          ; If MAP < threshold, reload timer!

MXSBST.overview: MXSBST_AllowedBoost_FromSpeed implements vehicle speed-dependent boost limiting (gear-based / traction boost limiting). In front-wheel-drive Chrysler turbo vehicles, hitting full 12+ psi boost in 1st gear causes uncontrollable wheelspin and violent torque steer. Additionally, on automatic transmission vehicles, full-boost low-speed launches cause severe torque converter and differential pin wear. MXSBST limits boost to 7.2 psi below 21 mph, allowing boost to ramp up to full 12.1 psi as vehicle speed crosses 30 mph.
MXSBST.overview_markdown:
`MXSBST_AllowedBoost_FromSpeed` implements **vehicle speed-dependent boost limiting (gear-based / traction boost limiting)**.

In front-wheel-drive Chrysler turbo vehicles, hitting full 12+ psi boost in 1st gear causes uncontrollable wheelspin and violent torque steer. Additionally, on automatic transmission vehicles, full-boost low-speed launches cause severe torque converter and differential pin wear. `MXSBST` limits boost to 7.2 psi below 21 mph, allowing boost to ramp up to full 12.1 psi as vehicle speed crosses 30 mph.
MXSBST.tuners_guide: 1st Gear Launch Traction: Excellent tool for dialing in launch traction on high-horsepower street cars. Manual vs. Automatic: On manual transmission calibrations, if the Park/Neutral switch or speed flag is grounded, this limiter may be bypassed. Drag Racing: If running drag slicks and you want full boost off the line, raise Point 1 to match your target boost so low speed does not hold back launch power.
MXSBST.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **1st Gear Launch Traction:** Excellent tool for dialing in launch traction on high-horsepower street cars.
* **Manual vs. Automatic:** On manual transmission calibrations, if the Park/Neutral switch or speed flag is grounded, this limiter may be bypassed.
* **Drag Racing:** If running drag slicks and you want full boost off the line, raise Point 1 to match your target boost so low speed does not hold back launch power.
MXSBST.operating_conditions:
* **Vehicle Speed Evaluation:**
  * In `CalcTargetBoost_MM`:
  * Only evaluated if port C indicates automatic transmission or speed-limiting flag is set (`andb #0x08`).
  * Clamps boost goal: $	ext{Temp4} = \min(	ext{Temp4}, 	ext{MXSBST}(	ext{VehicleSpeed}))$.

technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
ldab Z83_PortCdata    
        andb #0x08          ; Check speed limiter enable flag
        beq  LF2A9          ; If not enabled, skip!
        ldx  #MXSBST_AllowedBoost_FromSpeed
        ldd  VehicleSpeed_HB ; Read vehicle speed
        asld                ; Scale for table indexing
        asld
        asld
        jsr  LookupAndKeepSmallerBoostGoal ; Clamp to MIN(Temp4, MXSBST)

RATLIM.overview: RATLIM_BoostOverboostPrevention establishes an RPM-dependent rate-of-rise boost buffer used to prevent sudden boost spikes and overboost shutoff triggers. During rapid turbo spool-up in low gears, boost can spike past the target before the wastegate actuator can physically move. RATLIM models the maximum allowable rate of boost increase vs RPM, preemptively pulling wastegate duty cycle to cushion the spool curve and prevent slamming into the overboost fuel cut ceiling.

REVLMT.overview: REVLMT_OverRevFuelShutoff is the master engine redline rev limiter (fuel cut enable RPM). Protects the valvetrain from valve float, piston-to-valve contact, and rod bearing failure. On Chrysler distributor systems, the period timer measures time between ignition pulses (inversely proportional to RPM). REVLMT.overview_markdown:
`REVLMT_OverRevFuelShutoff` is the **master engine redline rev limiter (fuel cut enable RPM)**.

Protects the valvetrain from valve float, piston-to-valve contact, and rod bearing failure. On Chrysler distributor systems, the period timer measures time between ignition pulses (inversely proportional to RPM). When engine speed exceeds `REVLMT` (approx. 6490 RPM), the ECU immediately cuts fuel delivery to all injectors.
REVLMT.tuners_guide: Stock Cut Point: ~ 6490 RPM . Raising Redline: For modified engines with upgraded valve springs and performance camshafts, raise REVLMT to 6800-7200 RPM. Always raise REVLMT2 proportionally to ensure smooth fuel recovery.
REVLMT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Stock Cut Point:** $\approx 6490\text{ RPM}$.
* **Raising Redline:**
  * For modified engines with upgraded valve springs and performance camshafts, raise `REVLMT` to 6800–7200 RPM.
  * Always raise `REVLMT2` proportionally to ensure smooth fuel recovery.

WSGCHG.overview: WSGCHG_AllowedBoost_FromChargeTemp provides intake air charge temperature boost limiting. Compressed turbo air heats up dramatically. If the intake charge temperature becomes excessively hot (due to a heat-soaked intercooler, high ambient summer temps, or non-intercooled Turbo I configurations), the risk of catastrophic detonation skyrockets. WSGCHG senses charge temperature and pulls boost down (from 12.1 psi down to 7.6 psi) if intake air temps become dangerously elevated.
WSGCHG.overview_markdown:
`WSGCHG_AllowedBoost_FromChargeTemp` provides **intake air charge temperature boost limiting**.

Compressed turbo air heats up dramatically. If the intake charge temperature becomes excessively hot (due to a heat-soaked intercooler, high ambient summer temps, or non-intercooled Turbo I configurations), the risk of catastrophic detonation skyrockets. `WSGCHG` senses charge temperature and pulls boost down (from 12.1 psi down to 7.6 psi) if intake air temps become dangerously elevated.
WSGCHG.tuners_guide: Intercooler Health: If your car pulls hard on the first run down the drag strip but falls flat on subsequent runs, check charge temperatures. An undersized intercooler heat-soaks quickly, triggering WSGCHG boost reduction. High Boost Tuning: Remember to raise WSGCHG at normal operating voltages (above 0.3V) when increasing boost targets.
WSGCHG.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Intercooler Health:** If your car pulls hard on the first run down the drag strip but falls flat on subsequent runs, check charge temperatures. An undersized intercooler heat-soaks quickly, triggering `WSGCHG` boost reduction.
* **High Boost Tuning:** Remember to raise `WSGCHG` at normal operating voltages (above 0.3V) when increasing boost targets.
WSGCHG.operating_conditions:
* **Charge Temperature Evaluation:**
  * In `CalcTargetBoost_MM`:
  * Looked up using raw `ChargeTempVolts`.
  * Clamps boost goal: $	ext{Temp4} = \min(	ext{Temp4}, 	ext{WSGCHG}(	ext{ChargeTempVolts}))$.

ldx  #WSGCHG_AllowedBoost_FromChargeTemp
        ldaa ChargeTempVolts ; Read charge temp sensor ADC voltage
        jsr  LookupAndKeepSmallerBoostGoal ; Clamp to MIN(Temp4, WSGCHG)

WSGCLT.overview: WSGCLT_AllowedBoost_FromTemp is the engine thermal protection boost ceiling curve based on coolant temperature. High boost on a cold engine causes severe piston scuffing, head gasket failure, and high thermal shock. High boost on an overheating engine causes runaway detonation and pre-ignition. WSGCLT restricts boost to low spring pressure (approx. 5.5 psi) when the engine is cold (<100 degF) or overheating (>230 degF), only allowing full boost when coolant temperature is within safe operating range (120 degF-215 degF).
WSGCLT.overview_markdown:
`WSGCLT_AllowedBoost_FromTemp` is the **engine thermal protection boost ceiling curve based on coolant temperature**.

High boost on a cold engine causes severe piston scuffing, head gasket failure, and high thermal shock. High boost on an overheating engine causes runaway detonation and pre-ignition. `WSGCLT` restricts boost to low spring pressure (approx. 5.5 psi) when the engine is cold (<100°F) or overheating (>230°F), only allowing full boost when coolant temperature is within safe operating range (120°F–215°F).
WSGCLT.tuners_guide: Cold Engine Protection: Prevents drivers from beating on a cold engine before the oil and coolant have reached operating temperatures. Overheating Protection: Acts as an automatic failsafe if a radiator hose bursts or the thermostat sticks, dropping the car to mechanical wastegate boost to save the engine. Raising Boost: When raising maximum boost to 15+ psi, increase the plateau of WSGCLT (between 130 degF and 200 degF) to match your target, while maintaining low boost at cold and overheating extremes.
WSGCLT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Cold Engine Protection:** Prevents drivers from beating on a cold engine before the oil and coolant have reached operating temperatures.
* **Overheating Protection:** Acts as an automatic failsafe if a radiator hose bursts or the thermostat sticks, dropping the car to mechanical wastegate boost to save the engine.
* **Raising Boost:** When raising maximum boost to 15+ psi, increase the plateau of `WSGCLT` (between 130°F and 200°F) to match your target, while maintaining low boost at cold and overheating extremes.
WSGCLT.operating_conditions:
* **Thermal Clamp Check:**
  * In `CalcTargetBoost_MM`:
  * Looked up vs. `CoolantTemp`.
  * Clamps boost goal: $	ext{Temp4} = \min(	ext{Temp4}, 	ext{WSGCLT}(	ext{CoolantTemp}))$.

technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
ldx  #WSGCLT_AllowedBoost_FromTemp
        ldaa CoolantTemp    ; Read coolant temperature
        jsr  LookupAndKeepSmallerBoostGoal ; Clamp to MIN(Temp4, WSGCLT)

WSGKNK.overview: WSGKNK_BoostTimeSinceLastKnock defines the knock-triggered boost reduction penalty curve. When the piezoelectric knock sensor detects engine knock under boost, the ECU instantly retards ignition timing. If knock persists or exceeds knock thresholds, spark retard alone is insufficient. WSGKNK directly subtracts boost from the target boost goal immediately following a knock event, steadily restoring boost back to normal over a 2.8-second decay window as long as no further knock occurs.
WSGKNK.overview_markdown:
`WSGKNK_BoostTimeSinceLastKnock` defines the **knock-triggered boost reduction penalty curve**.

When the piezoelectric knock sensor detects engine knock under boost, the ECU instantly retards ignition timing. If knock persists or exceeds knock thresholds, spark retard alone is insufficient. `WSGKNK` directly **subtracts boost from the target boost goal** immediately following a knock event, steadily restoring boost back to normal over a 2.8-second decay window as long as no further knock occurs.
WSGKNK.tuners_guide: Stock Setting: Subtracts 2.1 psi boost immediately upon knock, decaying to 0 psi over ~2.8 seconds. Safety Failsafe: Protects the engine from repeating high-load detonation cycles. Tuning Note: Do not zero out WSGKNK on street engines running pump gas. If knock occurs, lowering boost is your best defense against broken ring lands and melted pistons.
WSGKNK.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Stock Setting:** Subtracts 2.1 psi boost immediately upon knock, decaying to 0 psi over ~2.8 seconds.
* **Safety Failsafe:** Protects the engine from repeating high-load detonation cycles.
* **Tuning Note:** Do not zero out `WSGKNK` on street engines running pump gas. If knock occurs, lowering boost is your best defense against broken ring lands and melted pistons.
WSGKNK.operating_conditions:
* **Post-Knock Subtraction:**
  * In `CalcTargetBoost_MM`:
  * `WSGKNK` is looked up using `Timer_Over5PSIBoost` (time elapsed since last knock event).
  * The penalty value is subtracted from the accumulated boost target:
    $$	ext{Final Boost Target} = \max(0, 	ext{Temp4} - 	ext{WSGKNK}(	ext{KnockTimer})) + 	ext{Baro}$$

technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
LF2A9:  ldx  #WSGKNK_BoostTimeSinceLastKnock
        ldaa Timer_Over5PSIBoost    ; Time since last knock event
        jsr  Lookup4ByteTable ; Look up boost subtraction penalty
        ldaa Temp4          ; Load accumulated boost goal
        sba                 ; A = Temp4 - WSGKNK penalty
        bcc  LF2B7          ; If >= 0, proceed
        clra                ; Else clamp to zero boost
LF2B7:  adda BaroPressure   ; Add barometric pressure to get absolute target

WSGKNK.calibration_notes: * This is a **subtraction table**, not a ceiling clamp table.
